rows.definition: The primary data processed or generated by the product is visual (images, video, or visual assets). True if the core function involves manipulating, analyzing, or delivering visual content. False if the core data is text, audio, or structured numerical data.
rows.name: Operates On Visual Media

rows.definition: The core value proposition is the automated execution of multi-step operational tasks (such as logistics coordination, record retrieval, or insurance verification) that were previously performed manually by human staff, reducing headcount or time-per-task.
rows.name: Operational Automation Agent

rows.definition: The product automates or manages internal business operations such as inventory, procurement, supply chain logistics, or manufacturing production lines. This is false if the product focuses on customer-facing interactions (support, sales) or consumer personal use.
rows.name: Operational Backend Automation

rows.definition: The core product ingests, normalizes, or routes transactional, operational, or telemetry data from multiple disparate sources to provide unified visibility or analytics.
rows.name: Operational Data Aggregator

rows.definition: The company's value delivery involves the physical movement, storage, or manufacturing of tangible goods, as opposed to purely digital information or software services.
rows.name: Physical Goods Fulfillment

rows.definition: The product involves physical hardware components that must be installed or integrated into existing physical infrastructure (e.g., vehicles, labs). True if the solution requires physical installation or hardware deployment. False if the product is purely software or digital services.
rows.name: Physical Hardware Integration

rows.definition: The company's primary value proposition is the design, manufacturing, or sale of tangible physical goods, as opposed to purely digital software, data, or services.
rows.name: Physical Product Manufacturer

rows.definition: The core product is a physical robotic system or hardware device that performs mechanical tasks, rather than a software-only solution.
rows.name: Physical Robotics Hardware

rows.definition: The product uses machine learning or AI primarily for prediction, classification, anomaly detection, or optimization of existing data, rather than generating new creative content.
rows.name: Predictive Or Analytical AI

rows.definition: The core technology involves ingesting, interpreting, or generating unstructured data such as video feeds, images, audio, or raw sensor inputs. It is false if the system primarily operates on tabular or text-based business records.
rows.name: Processes Unstructured Media Or Sensor Data

rows.definition: The company's core workflow involves ingesting, analyzing, or generating unstructured text data (e.g., emails, documents, code, invoices). True if the primary data input/output is text-based. False if the primary data is structured numerical data, images, or physical goods.
rows.name: Processes Unstructured Text Data

rows.definition: The product is a tool, library, framework, or API intended to be used by software engineers or data scientists to build other applications or models. This is true if the end-user is a technical builder. It is false if the product is a finished application for non-technical business users or consumers.
rows.name: Provides Developer Tooling

rows.definition: The product facilitates synchronous or near-synchronous interaction between multiple users, often involving voice, video, or shared state. This is true if the core experience is multi-user interaction (e.g., video messaging, multiplayer gaming). It is false if the product is primarily asynchronous, single-user, or a backend service.
rows.name: Real Time Collaboration Tool

rows.definition: The core workflow involves sourcing, screening, or matching candidates for employment roles.
rows.name: Recruiting Talent Acquisition

rows.definition: The core value proposition involves managing, anonymizing, securing, or processing data subject to strict regulatory compliance (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS) or sensitive PII/PHI. It is false if the data handled is public, non-sensitive, or if the product does not primarily concern data privacy/compliance.
rows.name: Regulated Data Handling

rows.definition: The primary customers operate in industries subject to heavy government regulation, such as healthcare, insurance, legal, or defense, requiring compliance-focused solutions.
rows.name: Regulated Industry Buyer

rows.definition: The core value proposition is the automation of tasks traditionally performed by human employees (such as customer support, code review, or operational analysis) using autonomous AI agents or models, rather than merely providing tools for humans to use.
rows.name: Replaces Human Labor With AI Agents

rows.definition: The core value proposition is the automation or outsourcing of administrative, clerical, or back-office tasks (e.g., bookkeeping, claims processing, invoice entry) that were previously performed by human staff, rather than providing a tool for humans to perform these tasks faster.
rows.name: Replaces Manual Back Office Operations

rows.definition: The product automates or streamlines administrative, financial, or operational back-office processes (e.g., tax filing, usage metering, rewards management) that were previously done manually by staff. It is false if the product primarily enhances front-facing customer interactions or physical infrastructure.
rows.name: Replaces Manual Back Office Tasks

rows.definition: The product automates a workflow that was traditionally performed by a specialized human professional (e.g., accountant, lawyer, researcher, teacher) rather than a general administrative task. It is false if it replaces a simple clerical task or creates a new capability that had no human equivalent.
rows.name: Replaces Professional Service

rows.definition: The core workflow involves identifying, quantifying, or reducing potential negative outcomes (security threats, financial risks, cyber liabilities) for the client.
rows.name: Risk Assessment And Mitigation

rows.definition: The product automates or enhances the workflow of identifying, contacting, or converting potential customers (leads). It is false if the product focuses on post-sale support, internal operations, or product development.
rows.name: Sales Marketing Automation

rows.definition: The product is designed to identify, prevent, or mitigate security threats, vulnerabilities, or risks to the customer's systems or people.
rows.name: Security Risk Mitigation

rows.definition: The product is designed for self-service use by end-users or business operators without the need for dedicated implementation consultants or custom development for each client.
rows.name: Self Service Software

rows.definition: The primary target customer base consists of large corporations, financial institutions, or major industrial players with complex compliance or scale requirements.
rows.name: Serves Large Enterprise Or Institutional Clients

rows.definition: The company's primary customers operate in sectors subject to strict government or industry compliance standards (e.g., FDA, GxP, financial regulations, healthcare licensing). It is false if the customers are in unregulated consumer or general B2B markets without specific compliance mandates.
rows.name: Serves Regulated Industry

rows.definition: True if the product is explicitly designed for or marketed to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMBs) as the primary customer segment. False if the primary customers are large enterprises, consumers, or government entities.
rows.name: Serves Small And Medium Businesses

rows.definition: The product is a platform designed to facilitate connections, interactions, or reputation building between users, typically involving user-generated profiles or content.
rows.name: Social Networking Platform

rows.definition: The product is a self-contained web or mobile application used directly by humans to perform tasks, without requiring integration into a third-party backend system to function. This is false if the product is primarily an API or backend service.
rows.name: Standalone End User Application

rows.definition: The primary input data consists of unstructured or semi-structured text documents (legislation, RFPs, medical records, code) that are parsed and analyzed.
rows.name: Structured Document Processing

rows.definition: The company operates within the logistics and freight industry, facilitating the movement of physical goods, managing carriers, or optimizing shipping routes.
rows.name: Supply Chain Logistics

rows.definition: The product focuses on improving the efficiency, cost, or reliability of the movement of goods or materials from source to end-user, including logistics and inventory management.
rows.name: Supply Chain Optimization

rows.definition: The primary function is to identify, vet, and connect human talent (employees, contractors) with employers, replacing traditional recruiting or job board workflows.
rows.name: Talent Matching Workflow

rows.definition: The primary buyers are large organizations, institutions, or enterprises (e.g., hedge funds, pharma companies, platform engineering teams) rather than individual consumers, small businesses, or independent contractors. It is false if the primary buyer is a sole proprietor, individual professional, or end-consumer.
rows.name: Targets Enterprise Or Institutional Buyers

rows.definition: True if the company generates revenue primarily through fees on transactions, interest on loans, or per-unit service charges. False if revenue is primarily from software subscriptions or licensing.
rows.name: Transaction Based Revenue

rows.definition: The company's primary revenue stream is derived from a percentage or fixed fee on financial transactions processed through its platform, rather than software licensing or subscription fees.
rows.name: Transaction Fee Model

rows.definition: The company utilizes artificial intelligence, machine learning, or large language models as a core component of its product to automate tasks, generate content, or make decisions. This is true if AI agents, models, or ML algorithms are central to the value proposition. It is false if the product relies primarily on deterministic rules, manual processes, or simple data aggregation without AI.
rows.name: Uses AI For Automation Or Decisioning

rows.definition: The core technology stack relies on generative AI models (LLMs, diffusion models, etc.) to create new content (text, video, code, or data structures) rather than merely analyzing existing data or automating deterministic rules.
rows.name: Uses Generative AI For Content Creation

rows.definition: The company targets a specific vertical industry (e.g., trucking, mortgage, mushroom farming) with specialized tools, rather than offering horizontal tools applicable to any industry.
rows.name: Vertical Specialization

rows.definition: The product acts as an autonomous or semi-autonomous agent that executes multi-step workflows, makes decisions, or completes tasks end-to-end on behalf of the user, reducing manual intervention.
rows.name: Workflow Automation Agent

rows.definition: The product simplifies a complex multi-step technical integration or configuration process by providing a unified interface, configuration language, or API that hides underlying complexity (e.g., multi-chain crypto, video AI context, enterprise app stacks).
rows.name: Abstracts Complex Integration

rows.definition: The primary function is to automate repetitive, rule-based, or document-heavy administrative tasks (such as scheduling, paperwork, or compliance checks) to reduce manual labor.
rows.name: Administrative Automation

rows.definition: The product deploys autonomous or semi-autonomous AI agents that execute multi-step business workflows (e.g., procurement, compliance, or data labeling) with minimal human intervention.
rows.name: AI Agent Workflow Automation

rows.definition: The core value proposition relies on machine learning or AI algorithms to optimize complex systems, generate strategies, or analyze data beyond simple rule-based logic.
rows.name: AI Driven Optimization

rows.definition: The core value proposition relies on machine learning or large language models to process unstructured data, automate complex reasoning, or generate content/code. False if the product is primarily a rule-based workflow, a static database, or a simple connectivity layer without AI inference.
rows.name: AI Driven Processing

rows.definition: The product utilizes Artificial Intelligence or Machine Learning to generate content, make decisions, or automate tasks that would otherwise require human input (e.g., generating voice, code, or predictions). It is false if the technology is purely deterministic, rule-based, or mechanical without an AI component.
rows.name: AI Generated Output

rows.definition: The product specifically optimizes, accelerates, or manages the process of training or running machine learning models, including hardware allocation, kernel optimization, or simulation of physical processes for AI.
rows.name: AI Model Training Optimization

rows.definition: The company employs AI models specifically for decision-making, reasoning, or complex problem-solving (such as optimization or contract logic) rather than just pattern matching or content generation.
rows.name: AI Reasoning Layer

rows.definition: The primary interface for interacting with the product is a programmatic API (REST, GraphQL, etc.) rather than a graphical user interface (GUI). This is true if the product is designed to be called by other software. It is false if the primary interaction is via a web dashboard or mobile app.
rows.name: API First Interface

rows.definition: The product is delivered primarily as a set of APIs, SDKs, or headless services intended to be integrated into other software systems, rather than as a standalone user-facing application with a primary GUI. This is false if the product is a self-contained web or mobile app used directly by humans without integration into other systems.
rows.name: API Or Headless Architecture

rows.definition: The company provides an API, SDK, or platform that other developers or businesses integrate into their own products. This is true if the product is consumed programmatically or as a white-label service. It is false if the product is a standalone end-user application.
rows.name: API Or Platform Model

rows.definition: The system primarily ingests, processes, or generates audio signals (speech, music, or sound effects) as its core data type.
rows.name: Audio Data Processing

rows.definition: The system performs multi-step tasks autonomously on behalf of the user, such as navigating websites, executing code, or preparing financial statements, with minimal human intervention in the execution phase.
rows.name: Automated Agent Execution

rows.definition: The product uses AI or machine learning to make or significantly assist in complex decisions (such as underwriting, forecasting, or risk assessment) that were previously done by humans. This is true if the AI is the core engine for the decision output. It is false if AI is only used for auxiliary tasks like search or chat.
rows.name: Automates Decision Making Via AI

rows.definition: The core value proposition involves automating tasks related to legal, financial, or regulatory compliance, such as AML checks, patent filings, or audit trails.
rows.name: Automates Regulatory Compliance

rows.definition: The product automates routine, high-volume operational tasks that were previously performed by humans, such as data entry, scheduling, or basic customer interactions. This is true if the core function is task automation (RPA, AI agents for calls, etc.). It is false if the product is primarily for analysis, design, or strategic decision-making.
rows.name: Automates Repetitive Operational Tasks

rows.definition: The primary product is a programmatic interface (API) or SDK intended for integration into other software systems, rather than a standalone user-facing application or physical good. It is true if the core value proposition is enabling other developers or systems to call the service. It is false if the primary interface is a consumer app, a physical device, or a manual service.
rows.name: B2B API Infrastructure

rows.definition: The primary customers are individual end-users purchasing the product or service for personal consumption, lifestyle, or health purposes.
rows.name: B2C Consumer Market

rows.definition: The company's core operations involve biological processes, genetic data, or biotechnology (e.g., fermentation, genomics, bioinformatics). It is false if the company operates purely in software, finance, or general industrial sectors without a biological component.
rows.name: Biotech Genomics Focus

rows.definition: The primary user interface and interaction surface is a web browser, including extensions or web apps, without requiring native desktop or mobile app installation for core functionality.
rows.name: Browser Based Application

rows.definition: The primary user interface is delivered via a web browser or a native mobile application, requiring no local desktop software installation or on-premise hardware setup for the end-user.
rows.name: Browser Or Mobile Native Interface

rows.definition: The primary user interface and delivery mechanism is a web browser, requiring no native desktop or mobile app installation for core functionality. It is false if the product requires a dedicated native application, hardware device, or on-premise server installation.
rows.name: Browser Web Delivery

rows.definition: The product's primary value proposition is ensuring adherence to specific legal, regulatory, or industry compliance standards (e.g., HIPAA, ADA, EEOC, SOC2, freight compliance). This is true if the software exists primarily to mitigate regulatory risk or prove diligence. It is false if the product is driven by efficiency, cost reduction, or user experience without a specific regulatory mandate.
rows.name: Compliance Regulation Driven

rows.definition: The primary workflow involves automating tasks related to legal compliance, regulatory filings, tax calculations, or industry-specific rules. This is true if the software reduces the burden of adhering to external regulations (e.g., titling, tariffs, healthcare standards). It is false if the workflow is focused on creative production, general analytics, or pure entertainment.
rows.name: Compliance & Regulatory Automation

rows.definition: The product is designed to ensure adherence to legal, regulatory, or contractual standards, or to mitigate financial and operational risks for the buyer.
rows.name: Compliance & Risk Management

rows.definition: The primary purchaser of the product or service is an individual consumer (B2C). This is true if the company sells directly to end-users for personal use. It is false if the primary revenue source is business entities (B2B).
rows.name: Consumer B2C Buyer

rows.definition: The primary revenue source is direct payments from individual end-users (freemium, subscription, or one-time purchase) for a product or service.
rows.name: Consumer Direct Seller

rows.definition: The primary end-user of the product is an individual consumer rather than a business entity. False if the product is sold to businesses for internal use or B2B services.
rows.name: Consumer Facing

rows.definition: The product provides a direct interface or service to individual end-users (consumers) rather than acting as a backend tool for businesses. It is false if the product is exclusively B2B infrastructure or internal tools not directly used by the final consumer.
rows.name: Consumer Facing Interface

rows.definition: The product serves personal lifestyle needs such as social discovery, grocery shopping, or health/wellness habits. This is true if the value proposition is personal convenience, social connection, or physical/mental well-being. It is false if the product serves business operational needs.
rows.name: Consumer Lifestyle Domain

rows.definition: The company operates a two-sided marketplace or platform where individual consumers transact directly with independent providers or other consumers, often taking a commission or fee per transaction, rather than selling a standardized product or service directly.
rows.name: Consumer Marketplace Transaction

rows.definition: The primary customer is an individual consumer, creator, or professional purchasing the product for personal use, client management, or direct service delivery to end-users, rather than an internal business tool.
rows.name: Consumer Or Creator Buyer

rows.definition: The company sells physical goods or digital content directly to individual end-users (B2C), typically via e-commerce or direct retail, rather than serving corporate clients.
rows.name: Consumer Product Sale

rows.definition: The primary revenue source is selling products or services directly to individual end-users (B2C), including physical goods or digital content subscriptions.
rows.name: Consumer Product Seller

rows.definition: The primary users are individual consumers (not businesses) who use the platform for social interaction, community building, or personal content sharing.
rows.name: Consumer Social Network

rows.definition: The product automates or assists in the creation of media assets (video, audio, or text) for marketing or communication purposes.
rows.name: Content Creation Automation

rows.definition: The product provides tools or platforms primarily for the creation, editing, or distribution of creative content (code, video, music, avatars) rather than for consumption or transactional processing.
rows.name: Content Creation Tooling

rows.definition: The primary user interaction involves browsing, voting, rating, or filtering existing content or items to find relevant matches, rather than creating new content or processing transactions.
rows.name: Content Discovery And Curation

rows.definition: The product is designed to help content creators, influencers, or brands manage their relationship with an audience or other creators, including monetization, discovery, or community management.
rows.name: Creator Economy Infrastructure

rows.definition: The product's primary function is to unify, index, or aggregate data or content from multiple disparate third-party sources or platforms into a single interface.
rows.name: Cross Platform Data Aggregation

rows.definition: The core value proposition involves collecting, aggregating, or visualizing operational data to provide insights, dashboards, or real-time status updates to the user.
rows.name: Data Analytics And Monitoring

rows.definition: The core function involves processing, structuring, or analyzing large datasets to extract insights, predictions, or structured information from unstructured or raw data. It is false if the product primarily executes actions without significant data analysis (e.g., simple transaction processing).
rows.name: Data Analytics Intelligence

rows.definition: The product primarily operates on structured or semi-structured business data (SQL, logs, transaction records) to provide insights, optimization, or decision support, rather than processing unstructured media like images or audio.
rows.name: Data Analytics Operations

rows.definition: The core value proposition involves collecting, structuring, or synthesizing raw data into a usable format (e.g., contact profiles, product catalogs, DNA sequences) for downstream consumption.
rows.name: Data Enrichment And Synthesis

rows.definition: The product is a foundational layer for moving, storing, or processing data (e.g., streams, pipelines, storage) rather than an application that generates insights or actions for a specific business function.
rows.name: Data Infrastructure Or Pipeline

rows.definition: The primary workflow involves ingesting raw data (documents, images, code, logs) and transforming it into structured, queryable, or usable formats. This is true if the product's main function is data transformation or extraction. It is false if the product is primarily a communication tool, a financial transaction processor, or a content consumption platform.
rows.name: Data Processing Pipeline

rows.definition: The product provides insights, recommendations, or synthesized information to assist human decision-makers, but does not automatically execute the final action or transaction.
rows.name: Decision Support System

rows.definition: The primary users and buyers are software engineers or technical teams who integrate the tool into their development workflow.
rows.name: Developer Buyer

rows.definition: The company provides tools, platforms, or infrastructure primarily used by software engineers, data scientists, or IT operations teams to build, deploy, or manage software systems. This is true if the target user is a technical professional working on code, infrastructure, or AI model deployment. It is false if the tool is for non-technical business users.
rows.name: Developer & Infrastructure Tools

rows.definition: The product is primarily consumed by software engineers or technical teams to build, manage, or deploy other software systems, APIs, or codebases.
rows.name: Developer Platform

rows.definition: The primary users/buyers are software engineers or technical teams integrating the tool into their development stack. It is true if the product requires coding knowledge to utilize effectively. It is false if the product is designed for non-technical business users.
rows.name: Developer Tech Buyer

rows.definition: The product is a digital interface (app, website, or widget) facilitating the discovery, purchase, or management of goods or financial assets. It is false if the product is a backend API, physical hardware, or a professional workflow tool.
rows.name: Digital Commerce Platform

rows.definition: The core value proposition involves the creation, curation, or distribution of digital media assets (audio, video, text, or images) for consumption or sharing, rather than processing structured business data.
rows.name: Digital Media Creation

rows.definition: The workflow involves converting, structuring, or automating processes around unstructured or semi-structured documents (legal, compliance, due diligence).
rows.name: Document Digitization

rows.definition: The primary data input or output involves the creation, parsing, management, or processing of structured or unstructured documents (PDFs, forms, contracts, returns).
rows.name: Document Processing

rows.definition: The product is designed to be integrated as a component (API, SDK, library) into another company's existing product or application, rather than standing alone as a complete end-user application.
rows.name: Embeddable Component

rows.definition: The product is delivered as a plugin, extension, or overlay that operates within a third-party application (e.g., Gmail, Slack, mobile OS) rather than requiring users to switch to a standalone native application or web portal for primary interaction.
rows.name: Embedded In Existing Workflow

rows.definition: The primary value proposition is enhancing the efficiency or capability of software developers or engineers. True if the tool is used by developers to build, test, or deploy software. False if the tool is used by non-technical staff (HR, Sales, Designers).
rows.name: Enables Developer Productivity

rows.definition: The primary workflow supported is finding, synthesizing, or answering questions based on existing knowledge bases or literature. True if the product aids in information retrieval and analysis. False if the product aids in transaction processing, signal transmission, or physical repair.
rows.name: Enables Research Discovery

rows.definition: The product directly mediates or improves interactions between a business and its end-users or customers (e.g., answering calls, conversational avatars, retention monitoring). It is false if the product is purely internal infrastructure or back-office tooling.
rows.name: Enhances Customer Facing Interactions

rows.definition: The product is designed to speed up, debug, or improve the software development lifecycle. True if the description mentions IDE, debugging, coding agents, or developer tools; false if the product is for non-technical users.
rows.name: Enhances Developer Productivity

rows.definition: The product is designed to help customers meet regulatory, compliance, or audit requirements, such as clinical trial oversight, financial transaction records, or data privacy standards.
rows.name: Enterprise Compliance Readiness

rows.definition: The primary target customers are mid-sized to large enterprises or established businesses with complex operational needs, rather than startups, SMBs, or consumers.
rows.name: Enterprise Mid Market Target

rows.definition: The product is designed to reduce operational costs, improve internal team productivity, or optimize internal business processes for enterprise clients.
rows.name: Enterprise Operational Efficiency

rows.definition: The sales process involves long cycles, procurement departments, and integration with existing enterprise systems (like EMRs or chip design tools), targeting large organizations rather than self-serve SMBs.
rows.name: Enterprise Sales Cycle

rows.definition: The product is architected to handle high-volume, high-concurrency workloads typical of large enterprises, often requiring on-premise, private cloud, or high-throughput cloud infrastructure.
rows.name: Enterprise Scale Deployment

rows.definition: The primary target market consists of large enterprises, corporations, or large-scale organizations with complex IT or operational needs.
rows.name: Enterprise Target Market

rows.definition: The product is designed to automate or streamline complex internal business processes (e.g., document signing, loan origination, freight booking) for organizations.
rows.name: Enterprise Workflow Automation

rows.definition: The primary workflow involves the movement, trading, or settlement of financial assets (currency, crypto, securities, or lease rights) between parties.
rows.name: Financial Asset Transaction

rows.definition: The product automates repetitive financial tasks such as reconciliation, payroll processing, or proposal generation. This is true if the primary value is reducing manual effort in financial or accounting processes. It is false if the product is a manual tool or focuses on non-financial automation.
rows.name: Financial Automation Workflow

rows.definition: The service directly intervenes in financial transactions to accelerate cash collection, reduce costs, or optimize borrowing terms for the user.
rows.name: Financial Cashflow Optimization

rows.definition: The primary data operated on or the primary asset managed is financial in nature, including cash, investments, wealth, or financial market data. This is true if the product's core function is to move, secure, analyze, or grow money. It is false if the product operates on non-financial data like text, images, or physical logistics.
rows.name: Financial Data & Asset Management

rows.definition: The primary customer is a financial institution, lender, or entity involved in capital markets, trading, or payment processing infrastructure.
rows.name: Financial Institution Intermediary

rows.definition: The product enables the creation, management, or distribution of financial instruments such as credit cards, debit cards, loans, or payment processing, often requiring banking partnerships or regulatory compliance.
rows.name: Financial Instrument Issuance

rows.definition: The company's core function involves processing, indexing, or analyzing structured financial market data (stock prices, filings, financial models). It is true if the product ingests or outputs financial instruments data. It is false if the company deals with general business data, health records, or consumer behavior data unrelated to capital markets.
rows.name: Financial Market Data Consumer

rows.definition: The product operates within the domain of financial management, including expense tracking, payment processing, trading, or investment analysis. It is false if the product deals with non-financial data such as health records, student grades, or general marketing leads.
rows.name: Financial Operations

rows.definition: The product structure involves the redistribution or sharing of financial costs or risks (such as insurance premiums or out-of-pocket expenses) between parties (e.g., employer and employee, or trader and counterparty). It is false if the product is a simple payment processor or ledger without risk transfer mechanisms.
rows.name: Financial Risk Sharing

rows.definition: The company facilitates financial transactions, advice, or access to capital, acting as an intermediary between capital providers and seekers or consumers and advisors.
rows.name: Financial Services Intermediation

rows.definition: The product operates within the financial technology sector, facilitating payments, debt collection, or financial transactions. This is true if the core function involves moving money or managing financial liabilities. It is false if the core function is operational software, healthcare, or physical goods.
rows.name: Fintech Payment Domain

rows.definition: The product relies on large language models, generative AI, or foundation models to create new content, code, designs, or agents, rather than just using traditional machine learning for classification or prediction.
rows.name: Generative AI Or Foundation Model Usage

rows.definition: The company explicitly targets a specific geographic region (e.g., Latin America, US) as its primary market, with operations or product features tailored to that region's specific infrastructure or regulations.
rows.name: Geographically Focused Market

rows.definition: The product is explicitly designed to facilitate transactions, services, or compliance across multiple national jurisdictions or borders. It is false if the product is restricted to a single country or region.
rows.name: Global Cross Border Operations

rows.definition: The company's service or product is delivered across multiple countries or regions, often requiring localized infrastructure, compliance, or logistics.
rows.name: Global Distribution Network

rows.definition: The primary deliverable includes physical hardware components (sensors, displays, robots, devices) that are essential to the product's function. It is false if the product is purely software or digital services without a proprietary hardware component.
rows.name: Hardware Centric Product Form

rows.definition: The product offering includes physical hardware components (such as devices or storage infrastructure) in addition to software or digital services.
rows.name: Hardware Hybrid Delivery

rows.definition: The product's functionality depends on interacting with physical hardware, sensors, or embedded systems, not just digital data.
rows.name: Hardware In The Loop

rows.definition: The primary product is a physical device or hardware system. This is true if the company manufactures or sells tangible equipment. It is false if the product is purely software, digital content, or a service.
rows.name: Hardware Product

rows.definition: The product is designed for use by licensed medical professionals or researchers in a clinical setting, dealing with patient care, diagnosis, or treatment protocols.
rows.name: Healthcare Clinical Workflow

rows.definition: The company operates in the healthcare sector, providing medical devices, diagnostics, or health monitoring solutions. True if the product is intended for medical use, diagnosis, or treatment support. False if the product is for general wellness, fitness, or non-medical purposes.
rows.name: Healthcare Medical Device

rows.definition: The product or service is specifically designed for, or primarily sold to, universities, colleges, or academic research institutions.
rows.name: Higher Education Focus

rows.definition: The software is a general-purpose tool (e.g., design, support, marketing analytics) that can be adopted by companies across various industries without significant vertical-specific customization.
rows.name: Horizontal Productivity Tool

rows.definition: The product is designed to augment human decision-making by providing recommendations, drafts, or alerts that require human review and final approval, rather than fully autonomous execution.
rows.name: Human In The Loop

rows.definition: The product's primary function is to manage who or what can access specific resources, enforce permissions, and audit actions, particularly in the context of digital identities or automated agents. It is false if the product does not primarily deal with authentication, authorization, or permissioning.
rows.name: Identity And Access Management

rows.definition: The primary value proposition is improving the efficiency, visibility, or coordination of internal business processes (such as HR, IT operations, or project management) for the client organization.
rows.name: Internal Operations Optimization

rows.definition: The primary value proposition is reducing or eliminating the need for human labor in specific operational tasks, often targeting tasks that were previously too expensive or tedious to automate.
rows.name: Labor Cost Automation

rows.definition: The system utilizes Large Language Models (LLMs) to perform autonomous reasoning, querying, or task execution (agentic workflows) rather than just simple text generation or classification. It is false if the AI component is limited to traditional ML models or simple rule-based automation.
rows.name: LLM Agentic Reasoning

rows.definition: The company's core workflow involves monitoring, detecting, responding to, or mitigating specific types of disruptions, risks, or failures. This is true for incident response, credit risk underwriting, or insurance risk assessment. It is false if the workflow is focused on creation (like content or code) or consumption (like food).
rows.name: Manages Incident Or Risk Lifecycle

rows.definition: The product functions as a search engine or comparison tool that aggregates listings or offers from multiple third-party providers into a single interface. It is true if the core function is comparing external inventory or services; false if the company produces the underlying goods or services itself.

rows.definition: The product is designed for use by banks, fintechs, or businesses engaged in financial transactions, lending, or payments. This is true if the domain is finance. It is false if the domain is healthcare, education, retail, or other sectors.
rows.name: Serves Financial Services

rows.definition: The product has significant sales to government agencies, defense departments, or public sector entities. This is true if government contracts or pre-orders are a major part of the revenue model. It is false if the product is sold exclusively to private commercial entities or consumers.
rows.name: Serves Government Or Defense

rows.definition: The primary customer is an industrial entity involved in physical production, extraction, or heavy manufacturing. This is true if the description mentions mining, automotive manufacturing, or industrial processes. It is false if the product is for software, services, or consumer goods.
rows.name: Serves Industrial Manufacturers

rows.definition: True if the primary customer is a business in a specific industrial, construction, or manufacturing sector purchasing goods or specialized services. False if the customer is a general tech company, a consumer, or a financial institution.
rows.name: Serves Industrial Or Specialized B2B

rows.definition: True if the primary customer is a marketing, growth, or brand team responsible for customer acquisition and visibility. False if the primary customer is a developer, finance team, or individual consumer.
rows.name: Serves Marketing Buyers

rows.definition: The product is designed for individuals or very small teams (1-5 people) who lack dedicated IT or operations staff, enabling them to perform tasks typically requiring larger organizational infrastructure. It is true if the description emphasizes solo operators, independent creators, or removing overhead for small-scale businesses.
rows.name: Serves Micro Enterprises Or Solo Founders

rows.definition: The primary customers are government agencies, municipalities, or public institutions.
rows.name: Serves Public Sector

rows.definition: The product is designed to be used within workflows that are subject to specific financial regulations (such as SEC, FINRA, or banking compliance), often requiring the vendor or the product to adhere to strict data handling, audit, or licensing standards.
rows.name: Serves Regulated Financial Operations

rows.definition: The primary customers are other software companies or developers who integrate the product into their own applications or platforms via APIs or SDKs.
rows.name: Serves Software Developers

rows.definition: The primary operational market or customer base is located in the United States. It is false if the primary market is international or other specific regions.
rows.name: Serves Us Market

rows.definition: The company sells the outcome of a physical or operational task (e.g., cleaning, maintenance) rather than selling software tools or data insights to be used by the client's staff.
rows.name: Service As A Service

rows.definition: The company acts as an intermediary or orchestrator that connects clients with third-party service providers (such as manufacturers, nurses, or suppliers) to complete physical or professional tasks, managing the workflow and quality control rather than performing the core service itself with internal staff.
rows.name: Service Facilitation Platform

rows.definition: The company generates revenue by billing for specific services, coaching programs, or physical goods delivered to the customer, rather than selling software access or facilitating third-party transactions.
rows.name: Service/Program Fee Model

rows.definition: The product provides a virtual environment or mathematical model to simulate real-world physical or logical systems (such as electrical circuits or biological processes) for analysis, testing, or design, without requiring physical instantiation.
rows.name: Simulation And Modeling

rows.definition: The product generates synthetic data, simulated populations, or virtual environments to model outcomes or behaviors, rather than relying solely on observed real-world data for its core output.
rows.name: Simulation Or Synthetic Data Generation

rows.definition: The primary customers are small to medium-sized businesses, often local or independent operators, rather than large enterprises or individual consumers.
rows.name: SMB Buyer

rows.definition: The primary target market consists of small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) or micro-enterprises, rather than large enterprises or individual consumers.
rows.name: SMB Target Market

rows.definition: The primary target market consists of small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) rather than large enterprises or individual consumers. It is true if the product is priced, packaged, and marketed for organizations with limited IT resources. It is false if the product targets large enterprises with dedicated IT teams or individual consumers.
rows.name: SMB Targeted

rows.definition: The primary buyers are small-to-medium enterprises (SMEs) or traditional brick-and-mortar retailers that need to restock inventory or manage supply chains.
rows.name: SME Retailer Supply

rows.definition: The system ingests, structures, or queries data that is inherently tied to physical geographic locations, maps, or real-world spatial coordinates.
rows.name: Spatial Data Processing

rows.definition: The product operates primarily on structured or semi-structured data (e.g., databases, spreadsheets, CRM records) to provide insights or answers.
rows.name: Structured Data Analysis

rows.definition: The core value proposition relies on managing, indexing, or querying structured relational or object-oriented data records.
rows.name: Structured Data Modality

rows.definition: The core value proposition involves monitoring, validating, or analyzing structured data pipelines, databases, or transactional records.
rows.name: Structured Data Operations

rows.definition: The system primarily ingests and analyzes structured or semi-structured records (such as financial transactions, database entries, or sensor data) to derive insights. It is false if the system primarily processes unstructured text, images, or video.
rows.name: Structured Record Analysis

rows.definition: The primary data input processed by the system is structured numerical data, time-series, or IoT sensor telemetry. It is false if the primary input is unstructured text, images, or video.
rows.name: Structured Telemetry Data Processing

rows.definition: The company addresses inefficiencies or compliance risks in global trade, logistics, or supply chain documentation (e.g., tariffs, customs, quality control).
rows.name: Supply Chain Compliance Optimization

rows.definition: The core product addresses the physical movement, tracking, or management of goods and materials, including shipping, delivery, or inventory supply for businesses.
rows.name: Supply Chain Logistics Operations

rows.definition: The company operates within the physical supply chain, manufacturing, or industrial goods sector, dealing with the sourcing, production, or logistics of physical items.
rows.name: Supply Chain Manufacturing

rows.definition: The product facilitates the hiring, onboarding, or management of human resources, including recruiting, employer-of-record services, or employee benefits.
rows.name: Talent Acquisition & HR

rows.definition: The primary economic buyer or user of the product is a member of the finance, accounting, or revenue operations department, as opposed to engineering, sales, or marketing teams.
rows.name: Target Buyer Is Finance Or Revenue Team

rows.definition: The primary problem solved is improving the efficiency, capability, or experience of software developers or technical engineers. True if the user is a developer and the value is in coding, debugging, or infrastructure management. False if the user is a non-technical business user, consumer, or physical worker.
rows.name: Targets Developer Productivity

rows.definition: The primary buyer is a corporate security or IT infrastructure team responsible for protecting digital assets, network integrity, or data pipelines. It is false if the buyer is a consumer, a small business owner, or a non-technical department like HR or Sales.
rows.name: Targets Enterprise Security Operations

rows.definition: The primary customer base or use case is within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or healthcare research sectors. It is false if the product is designed for non-medical industries.
rows.name: Targets Healthcare Or Biotech Sector

rows.definition: The core problem addressed is related to public health, sanitation, hygiene, or medical outcomes. This is true if the description mentions health equity, sanitation, water filtration, or healthcare. It is false if the problem is commercial, technical, or educational.
examples: Sanitation and Health Rights in India (SHRI)
rows.name: Targets Healthcare Or Sanitation

rows.definition: The company explicitly targets the Indian market as its primary or exclusive geographic focus. This is true if the description highlights India as the key market or if the product is tailored specifically for Indian regulations/users. It is false if the company targets global or other specific regional markets without a primary focus on India.
rows.name: Targets Indian Market

rows.definition: The primary customer base or use case is within industrial distribution, manufacturing, or heavy machinery sectors. It is false if the product is designed for service, retail, or consumer industries.
rows.name: Targets Industrial Or Manufacturing Sector

rows.definition: The product is specifically designed for use in manufacturing, industrial operations, or physical goods production. This is true if the customers are factories, manufacturers, or industrial enterprises. It is false if the product is for software, services, or consumer sectors.
rows.name: Targets Manufacturing Or Industrials

rows.definition: The primary end-user or buyer is a professional engaged in scientific discovery, medical diagnosis, or clinical research, requiring high-precision information retrieval or specialized domain tools. It is true if the description identifies researchers, doctors, or scientists as the core user base.
rows.name: Targets Scientific Or Clinical Researchers

rows.definition: The primary input data processed by the product consists of text-based communications, such as chat messages, reviews, or written applications.
rows.name: Textual Communication Data

rows.definition: The company operates as a payment or financial infrastructure provider, earning revenue through transaction processing, interchange, or financial services fees rather than software licensing.
rows.name: Transaction Based Fintech

rows.definition: The primary revenue model is based on transactions, commissions, or fees per event (e.g., per trade, per policy, per delivery). This is true if the company earns money when a specific financial or physical transaction occurs. It is false if the revenue is primarily subscription-based.
rows.name: Transactional Or Commission Based Revenue

rows.definition: The company explicitly targets or restricts its operations, supply chain, or customer base to the United States, often citing domestic manufacturing, US-based teams, or US-specific regulatory compliance as a key feature.
rows.name: US Domestic Focus

rows.definition: The primary goal is to improve user retention, engagement, or response rates through automated communication or interaction strategies.
rows.name: User Retention And Engagement

rows.definition: The core technology or a significant portion of the product is open-source, allowing users to inspect, modify, or self-host the code. This is true if the company explicitly markets open-source components or licenses. It is false if the product is proprietary closed-source software.
rows.name: Uses Open Source Core

rows.definition: The core technology relies on mathematical optimization, search algorithms, or simulation to find the best parameters or configurations within a defined space. It is false if the primary mechanism is generative creation or simple rule-based automation.
rows.name: Uses Optimization Algorithms

rows.definition: The core technology relies on the acquisition, filtering, or interpretation of analog or digital signals (e.g., neural, audio, video) rather than purely symbolic or text-based processing. True if signal processing is the primary technical challenge. False if the primary challenge is text generation or database querying.
rows.name: Uses Signal Processing

rows.definition: The solution depends on proprietary hardware, physical engineering, or specialized scientific processes (e.g., satellite orbits, food chemistry) rather than purely software algorithms. It is false if the solution is implemented entirely in software on general-purpose computing hardware.
rows.name: Uses Specialized Hardware Or Physics

rows.definition: The product analyzes, curates, or generates short-form video content, often using algorithms to understand trends, virality, or user engagement. It is false if the product deals with text, audio, or static images as the primary modality.
rows.name: Video Content Analytics

rows.definition: The primary input data processed by the system is visual media, such as images, video feeds, or CAD models, used for perception or analysis.
rows.name: Visual Media Data

rows.definition: The primary data input or output involves images, video, 3D scans, or spatial mapping of the physical world.
rows.name: Visual Spatial Data

rows.definition: The primary interaction modality for the end-user or the automated agent is spoken language (voice), either for human-to-human communication or human-to-AI interaction.
rows.name: Voice Agent Interface

rows.definition: The company's primary function involves ingesting, parsing, or structuring unstructured data from public websites or the open web for downstream use.
rows.name: Web Data Extraction

rows.definition: The product's core function involves retrieving, aggregating, or enriching data from public or semi-public web sources (scraping, search, monitoring). It is false if the data is primarily generated internally by the user or comes from private, non-web databases.
rows.name: Web Scraping And Enrichment

rows.definition: The company utilizes WhatsApp as a primary channel for customer interaction, order placement, or service delivery, leveraging the messaging platform's ubiquity in specific markets.
rows.name: WhatsApp Native Channel

rows.definition: The company provides its software or service infrastructure for other organizations to rebrand and offer under their own name. It is true if the product is sold as a platform for third-party branding; false if the company sells under its own brand directly to end-users.
rows.name: White Label Licensing

rows.definition: The product is a platform that allows third parties to rebrand and embed the service into their own websites or products, acting as a backend engine for the customer's frontend.
rows.name: White Label Platform
